summary: IPinfo is a REST API for IP intelligence: geolocation, ASN, anonymity/hosting flags, company, and related data for IPv4/IPv6 addresses. It has tiers (Lite free, Core, Plus, Max), a batch endpoint, and a legacy API on ipinfo.io. Database downloads are also offered.

sources.quote: IPinfo Lite uses the api.ipinfo.io API URL and /lite endpoint.

value.description: API token passed as a query parameter (one of three accepted methods).
HTTP Basic with token as username and empty password.

sources.quote: HTTP Basic Authentication (using the token as the username, e.g. curl -u $TOKEN:)
A Bearer token in the Authorization header (Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN)

value.purpose: Free country/continent/ASN lookup; {ip} may be 'me'; optional /{field} suffix returns plaintext field.
Paid (Core/Plus/Max) lookup: geo, AS, network flags.
Up to 1,000 lookups/URL patterns in one request; returns JSON keyed by input. Also /batch/lite and /batch/legacy.

keyParams.name: body
keyParams.description: JSON array, newline- or space-separated list of IPs or patterns like lite/8.8.4.4/country

sources.quote: The /batch API endpoint lets you group up to 1,000 IPinfo API requests into a single HTTP request.

value.limits: Lite unlimited; paid plans have a monthly request quota; no daily/hourly caps, concurrency limits, or per-second throttling on paid plans.
value.description: Exceeding the plan limit returns HTTP 429 unless metered billing (overages) is enabled.

sources.quote: If you exceed your plan's limit, you'll receive a 429 HTTP status code.

value.description: No explicit version number; the endpoint name (lite, lookup) acts as the schema, and a legacy API remains on ipinfo.io.

sources.quote: Our legacy API is still maintained with fresh data

versioning.reasoning: Docs describe an updated api.ipinfo.io schema versus a legacy ipinfo.io schema, but give no versioning or deprecation policy.

risks.title: Two API generations
risks.detail: Updated (api.ipinfo.io) and legacy (ipinfo.io) have different response shapes; pick one deliberately.

risks.title: Free tokens can't use /lookup
risks.detail: Free tokens get an error on /lookup and default /batch; use /lite and /batch/lite.

risks.title: Token in query string
risks.detail: The token can leak in logs and URLs; prefer the Bearer header server-side. JSONP/CORS use exposes tokens in client code.

risks.title: Error format undocumented
risks.detail: Only 429 is mentioned; error bodies are not described in the fetched pages.

risks.title: Page truncation
risks.detail: Some fetched pages were truncated, so details may be missing.
